segments.text: On today's podcast we talk about scaling an early stage startup.
Our guest founded a developer tools company three years ago.
She says the first hire after product market fit was a support engineer.
Support surfaced the bugs that were quietly driving churn.
They kept the team under ten people until revenue was predictable.
Predictable revenue meant three months of stable net retention.
The biggest mistake was hiring salespeople before the product could sell itself.
She recommends founders do sales themselves for the first year.
On fundraising she raised a seed round of two million dollars.
The seed round gave them eighteen months of runway.
They avoided raising a large series A until growth was clearly repeatable.
Culture wise she protected engineering focus time aggressively.
No meetings before noon became a simple but powerful rule.
Her advice to new founders is to talk to customers every single week.
She closes by saying durability beats hypergrowth for most companies.
